We need to use integration by parts. We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=3{x}^{2}\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=6x \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x).\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula for integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 3{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(3{x}^{2})(\operatorname{sin}⁡(x))-\int (\operatorname{sin}⁡(x))(6x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)-6\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Again, we use integration by parts to evaluate $\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x & \,⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x) & \,⟹\,v=\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\text{d}x=-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x).\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x(-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))-\int (-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))\cdot 1\,dx \\  & =-x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,dx \\  & =-x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant. 

So, we get that the indefinite integral is

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 3{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =3{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)-6\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)-6(-x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+D) \\  & =3{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+6x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)-6\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=-6D.$

Finally, we can work out the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }3{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & ={[3{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+6x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)-6\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)]}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =(3(\pi )^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )+6(\pi )\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )-6\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi ))-(3(0)^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)+6(0)\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)-6\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)) \\  & =0+6\pi (-1)-0-0 \\  & =-6\pi \end{aligned}
$$
